pairs.subject: generator-uncertainty-scoring
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/scores.rs:1 The evaluation API ingests, reviews and gates on judge verdicts. Its only agreement signal is judge-vs-itself (scores_review low_agreement), and its only confidence bound is the run's CI on the judged mean (prompts_gate). A search of crates/api/src found no logprob, token-probability, generator self-consistency or gen_samples construct, so no judge-free generator-uncertainty score enters this context.

pairs.subject: generator-uncertainty-scoring
pairs.evidence: crates/runner/src/stats.rs:118 stability() returns a perfect 1.0 when fewer than two samples exist. compare.rs:736/775 applies it to the generator's candidate scores and writes gen_agreement unconditionally, so every single-draw case (or a cell left with one surviving candidate) records a confident zero-variance generator agreement where the technique requires an absence.

techniques.evidence: crates/runner/src/stats.rs:118 N<2 gives 1.0 instead of an absence. This value becomes per-case gen_agreement at compare.rs:775 even when n_candidates is 1. A second frame issue: compare.rs:739 switches the run-level 'agreement' field between generator stability (ng>1) and judge agreement (ng==1), so one field name carries two quantities. On the plus side, cli.rs:173-174 does declare the gate frame (draws are averaged 'to average out generation variance').

crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:5 The metered tier-2 judge scores production traces asynchronously: only settled traces, on a stable 1/N sample, never in the serving path. That matches the invariant binding absolutely at tier 2. No tier-0 or tier-1 production scorer is offered, and no logprob is read anywhere in the repo.

pairs.registryProposal: Consider naming a failure mode beside 'the frame collision': a single headline field whose source switches on a run parameter (generator spread when N>1, judge self-agreement when N=1). It is a frame swap driven by configuration rather than by an unlabelled number, and the techniques do not currently describe it.
